issues.description: CHANGELOG entry name doesn't match check name in the code
issues.detail: The CHANGELOG lists `compute_instance_single_network_interface` but the PR title and description say `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`. The actual check directory/class uses `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. Naming is inverted relative to intent (the check fails on multiple NICs, so name should reflect the rule clearly). At minimum, verify the check name matches what's documented and registered in the check registry.

issues.description: GKE-name heuristic is spoofable and not documented in metadata
issues.detail: Using `instance.name.startswith("gke-")` to grant MANUAL status is a weak signal — any user can name a VM `gke-foo` to evade FAIL. A more reliable signal would be checking instance labels (e.g., `goog-gke-node`) or the managed instance group. The metadata.json also doesn't document the MANUAL/GKE-exception behavior described in the check docstring.

issues.description: Zero-interface case silently emits PASS status
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, the report keeps `status = "PASS"` (from the default) while reporting "has no network interfaces". This is an unexpected/unreachable state in practice, but emitting PASS for it is misleading. Should be MANUAL or explicitly handled, and there is no test covering this branch.

issues.description: Mutable default value in Pydantic model field
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a mutable default. While Pydantic BaseModel typically handles this safely via field copying, it's an inconsistent style — other list-typed fields in this file should be checked. Prefer `Field(default_factory=list)` for clarity and safety against future Pydantic v2 strictness.

Splitting on `/` and taking `[-1]` extracts just the resource name, discarding the project/region context. Two networks with the same short name in different projects would collide. Consider storing the full self-link or both fields. Also, NetworkInterface name defaults to empty string — `nic0` is the GCP default, so `name=""` could be misleading in output.

issues.description: Test for no-instances case doesn't mock project_ids
issues.detail: The `test_compute_no_instances` test sets `compute_client.instances = []` but doesn't set `project_ids`. Since MagicMock auto-attributes, this works incidentally, but it's inconsistent with other tests that explicitly set `project_ids`. Also, no test covers a multi-NIC instance whose name happens to start with `gke-` but isn't actually a GKE node — the spoofability gap noted above.

review.summary: This PR adds a sensible GCP check for VMs with multiple network interfaces, with reasonable test coverage. Main concerns: the CHANGELOG/PR-title naming is inconsistent with the actual check name (`single` vs `multiple`); the GKE detection uses a trivially spoofable name prefix instead of labels/metadata; the zero-interface case silently passes; and the network URL parsing drops project context. Tests cover the main paths but miss the zero-NIC and spoofed-gke-name edge cases.
